spec.concept: Each half-life removes half of what's left, so decay never hits zero in a straight line.
spec.definition: Half-life is the time it takes for half of a radioactive sample's atoms to decay.

prediction.prompt: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years. How many years until only 10% of it is left in a bone?

extremes.watch: With a 1,000-year half-life, 10% is left after only about 3,322 years.
With a 10,000-year half-life it takes about 33,219 years.

misconceptions.label: 90% gone in under two half-lives
misconceptions.why_tempting: Half in 5,730 years makes 90% feel close behind.
misconceptions.refutation: Each half-life halves what's left: 50, 25, 12.5 percent, so 10% takes about 3.3 half-lives (19,000 years).
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Takes ten half-lives
misconceptions.why_tempting: Getting to 10% sounds like it should take ten steps.
misconceptions.refutation: Halving is fast: three halvings already reach 12.5%.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
